profile.summary: MP-RNA is an RNA foundation model that reads an RNA sequence one base at a time and produces representations for downstream prediction. It was pretrained on plant transcriptomes from over 1,000 species with objectives that include predicting secondary structure and repairing single-base mutations. It is aimed at tasks that need per-base resolution, such as RNA secondary structure prediction and mutation detection, and the authors also apply it to DNA tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: MP-RNA is a transformer encoder that reads RNA one base at a time. It is pretrained with three combined objectives: masked RNA language modelling, single nucleotide mutation repair (5% of sites are mutated and the model learns to correct them), and secondary structure prediction. Structure labels come from ViennaRNA. To limit noise from these computed labels, the authors keep the 10% of samples with the lowest expected calibration error for incremental pretraining, and append structures to the sequence in 10% of masked language modelling examples. After pretraining, the model is fine-tuned or used for tasks such as secondary structure prediction, mutation detection and repair, and DNA genomic tasks.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper describes two sizes, MP-RNA-52M and MP-RNA-186M, both pretrained on four RTX 4090 GPUs over one month. This page read one checkpoint, yangheng/MP-RNA; its configuration (32 layers, dimension 720) and parameter count match the 186M version. The paper states that only MP-RNA-186M received incremental pretraining and that the incrementally pretrained 52M model will not be released. Whether any other MP-RNA checkpoint is public was not checked. The paper and card link to github.com/yangheng95/OmniGenomeBench; the code repository read here is yangheng95/OmniGenBench, and no saved file shows how the two addresses are related. Its README's examples use OmniGenome models and list MP-RNA as one supported model. A result should name the Hugging Face revision; this page read revision 0a727ebb.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: RNA foundation model (masked language model with structure-aware pretraining objectives) used for RNA and DNA sequence tasks.
facts.source_locator: Model card: Model Description; paper Section 3.2

quotes.text: **MP-RNA** is a multi-species RNA foundation model designed to enhance the performance of in-silico RNA genomic tasks.
secondary structure prediction (SSP), single nucleotide mutation repair (SNMR), and masked RNA language modeling (MRLM)

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with rotary position embeddings. MP-RNA-186M: 32 layers, dimension 720, 30 heads; MP-RNA-52M: 16 layers, dimension 480, 24 heads. The released config uses custom OmniGenome model code (OmniGenomeForMaskedLM).

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: RNA (or DNA) sequences tokenised one base per token (single-nucleotide tokenisation), from a vocabulary that also includes secondary-structure symbols.
facts.source_locator: Paper Section 3.1; model card: How to use

quotes.text: we adopt SNT and represent the input tokens as individual bases
to unify the tokenization of both nucleotide bases and RNA secondary structure information.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-base hidden representations from the base model; with task heads, predictions such as secondary structure (dot-bracket labels in the config), mutation detection and repair, or sequence-level properties.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Plant transcriptome data from the OneKP initiative, covering 1,124 plant species (54.2B tokens of mRNA, CDS and UTRs per the paper's comparison table), sliced into 1,024-base windows, deduplicated, and filtered to remove sequences under 50 bases. Secondary structures were annotated with ViennaRNA.

run_guide.summary: Load the MP-RNA checkpoint from Hugging Face and run it on one short RNA sequence.
prerequisites: Python with the transformers package and PyTorch, which the card's example imports and returns tensors for. The card gives no install command or version.
Internet access to download yangheng/MP-RNA. The weights are Apache-2.0 and not gated.
Hardware needs for inference are not stated. The authors pretrained on four RTX 4090 GPUs.

steps.title: Load the model and run one sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

# Load pre-trained model tokenizer
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("yangheng/MP-RNA")

# Load pre-trained model
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("yangheng/MP-RNA")

# Example input sequence
input_seq = "AUGGCUACUUUCG"

# Tokenize input
inputs = tokenizer(input_seq, return_tensors="pt")

# Perform inference
outputs = model(**inputs)
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's example, unchanged, wrapped in a shell heredoc. The card does not pass trust_remote_code, although config.json points to custom model code.

notes: This page is meant for both MP-RNA records (lit-microbial-20261011-virobench-model-mp-rna and lit-rna-20261011-rnalm-zeroshot-model-mp-rna). The paper source is the pdftotext text layer of the ACL Anthology PDF (CC BY 4.0); the PDF itself is kept as artifacts/paper.pdf. The README examples use yangheng/OmniGenome-186M; no saved source links OmniGenome models to MP-RNA, so they are not treated as MP-RNA checkpoints. The saved GitHub API response artifacts/gh-repo-omnigenomebench.json gives yangheng95/OmniGenBench; no saved file shows how it relates to the OmniGenomeBench address the paper gives. That repository is treated as the code source. The cited paper file is the pdftotext text layer, so its sha256 is not the PDF's.
